title: Major burns
stem: Resus 1. A 30-year-old woman (about 70 kg) was trapped for around 30 minutes in a burning flat before firefighters carried her out an hour ago. She is drowsy, GCS 13. HR 124, BP 96/58, RR 26, SpO2 97% on a non-rebreather. Manage her initial resuscitation.
notes:
Checked against ATLS 11th edition, the British Burn Association / NHS burns referral guidance, ABA guidelines (2022 referral criteria) and current UK and HK practice for inhalation injury and carbon monoxide.

Inhalation injury: enclosed space, reduced consciousness, facial burns, singed nasal hair, soot in the mouth or sputum, hoarseness or stridor, and a raised carboxyhaemoglobin. Intubate early with an uncut tube (at least 7.5 in an adult) by the most experienced operator; swelling peaks over 24–48 hours. Suxamethonium is safe in the first 24 hours.

Pulse oximetry reads carboxyhaemoglobin as oxyhaemoglobin: SpO2 is falsely normal. Give 100% oxygen and measure COHb on a co-oximeter gas. Suspect cyanide (lactate over 8 mmol/L, shock, arrest) in enclosed-space fires: hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV.

Burn size counts partial- and full-thickness burns only (not erythema): rule of nines in adults, Lund–Browder in children, the patient's palm and fingers ≈ 1% for scattered burns. Formal fluids for over 20% TBSA in adults (over 10% in children) — ATLS, and your department's burn-unit threshold. UK/NICE practice starts at 15% in adults.

Fluids: ATLS 10th/11th uses 2 mL/kg/%TBSA of Hartmann's for adults (3 mL for children, 4 mL for electrical injury), half in the first 8 hours from the time of the burn, not arrival. Titrate to urine output 0.5 mL/kg/h (1 mL/kg/h in children). The station scores 2 mL/kg/%TBSA only; 4 mL is marked wrong. Naming: the original Parkland formula is 4 mL/kg/%; the 2 mL starting rate is ATLS 10th's modified version (the 'modified Parkland' / Brooke range), so say 'ATLS 2 mL/kg/%' in the exam. The formula is a starting point: over-resuscitation ('fluid creep') causes compartment syndromes.

Dressings: your notes say sterile moist dressings. That is fine for a small burn, and first-aid cooling (running water for 20 minutes within 3 hours) is correct. For a large burn like this one (36%), ATLS says cover with clean, dry, warm sheets or cling film: large wet dressings cool the patient fast, and hypothermia worsens coagulopathy and mortality. Cling film is also non-adherent, eases pain, and lets the burns team see the wound without taking a dressing off. Lay it in strips; don't wrap it round a limb.

Your department's criteria (Burn Unit: over 20% adults / 10% children under 12, inhalation needing ICU, major functional or cosmetic, comorbidity; Burn Facility: extremes of age, over 5%, special areas, comorbidity, chemical, circumferential, electrical, full thickness) broadly match international guidance. Missing compared with ABA 2022 / EMSB: burns with major trauma, suspected non-accidental injury, pregnancy, and all inhalation injury (not only ICU cases). This patient meets the Burn Unit criteria.

Referral: your notes list the older criteria (3rd degree over 5%, 20% combined, 10% in the young and old). Current ABA and UK guidance refer any full-thickness burn, partial-thickness over 10% (adults) or 5% (children), burns of the face, hands, feet, genitals, perineum or major joints, circumferential burns, inhalation injury, electrical and chemical burns, and burns with trauma or significant comorbidity.

steps.label: Get the bay ready
steps.hint: Trauma/burns call, PPE, difficult airway kit with uncut tubes, warm room, cling film.

opts.t: Trauma team and anaesthetist now
opts.mark: Calls the trauma team and anaesthetist early

opts.t: PPE
Difficult airway trolley with uncut size 7.5 and 8.0 tubes
opts.mark: Prepares for a difficult airway with uncut tubes

opts.t: Warm the room, warm fluids, warm blankets
Cling film and burns chart
opts.mark: Cling film and a burns chart ready

opts.t: Cold wet towels over all the burns
opts.r: Wet dressings over a large area make her hypothermic. Cooling helps only small burns in the first 3 hours.

steps.label: Handover
steps.hint: Enclosed space? Time of the burn? Loss of consciousness? What was given?

Fire.t: Where was she, and for how long?
Fire.r: Trapped in a smoke-filled bedroom, door shut, about 30 minutes.
Fire.mark: Asks about an enclosed space and duration

Fire.r: Fire started about 19:05. We got her out at 19:35. Now 20:05.
Fire.mark: Establishes the time of the burn

Fire.r: Unresponsive when we found her, woke up in the ambulance.

Treatment.r: Oxygen by mask. Nothing else. No cooling — too big an area.

Treatment.t: Any other injury, falls or explosion?

steps.label: Primary survey
steps.hint: Airway signs of inhalation, breathing, circulation, D, then expose and map the burn.

Airway.t: Look at the face, nose and mouth
Airway.r: Facial erythema, singed nasal hair and eyebrows, soot on the tongue and palate.
Airway.mark: Finds signs of inhalation injury (singed hair, soot)

Airway.t: Listen to her voice and breathing
Airway.r: Hoarse voice. Soft inspiratory stridor now.
Airway.mark: Recognises hoarseness and stridor as airway threat

Breathing.r: Partial-thickness burns on the chest, not circumferential. Scattered wheeze. RR 26.

Circulation.r: Two 16 G cannulae through unburnt skin in the left forearm and right foot.
Circulation.mark: IV access, through unburnt skin if possible

D E.r: GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6). Pupils equal. Glucose 6.2.

D E.t: Expose fully and map the burns
D E.r: Face red only. Chest, abdomen and left arm: blistered, pink, painful (partial thickness). Right arm: white, leathery, painless, circumferential (full thickness).
D E.mark: Maps burn depth and extent on a chart

D E.r: Rings and watch off before the hands swell.

steps.label: The airway
steps.hint: Stridor and hoarseness with soot: intubate early, uncut tube, most experienced operator.

opts.t: Intubate now, before the swelling: most experienced operator, uncut 8.0 tube
opts.mark: Early intubation with an uncut tube
opts.r: Anaesthetist: Agreed. Videolaryngoscope, uncut 8.0. Swollen but through. ETCO2 trace present.

opts.t: Watch her; intubate if the stridor gets worse
opts.r: By then the airway may be impossible. Swelling peaks over 24–48 hours.

opts.t: Avoid suxamethonium — it causes hyperkalaemia in burns
opts.r: Suxamethonium is safe in the first 24 hours. The risk starts after 24–48 hours.

steps.label: Investigations
steps.hint: A co-oximetry gas (COHb, lactate), ECG, chest film, bloods and group.

Gas.t: Arterial or venous gas with co-oximetry
Gas.r: COHb 22%. Lactate 5.8. pH 7.29. PaO2 on oxygen 38 kPa.

Other.t: FBC, U&E, CK, group and save, pregnancy test
Other.mark: Baseline bloods including CK and pregnancy test

Other.t: Trust the SpO2 of 97%: no gas needed
Other.r: Pulse oximetry reads carboxyhaemoglobin as oxygenated haemoglobin. It is falsely reassuring.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: 100% oxygen, analgesia, tetanus; hydroxocobalamin only if cyanide is suspected.

opts.t: 100% oxygen (ventilator FiO2 1.0)
Morphine IV, titrated
Tetanus booster if not up to date
Hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV if the lactate rises or she stays shocked
Prophylactic IV antibiotics
opts.r: Not indicated for fresh burns; they select resistant organisms.

opts.t: Dexamethasone for the airway swelling
opts.r: No evidence in inhalation injury; it increases infection.

steps.label: Fluid plan
steps.hint: TBSA counts partial and full thickness only. 2 mL × kg × %TBSA, half by 8 hours from the burn.

opts.t: TBSA 36% (chest 9, abdomen 9, both arms 18; the face is erythema only)
2 × 70 × 36 = 5040 mL Hartmann's in 24 h; 2520 mL by 8 h after the burn (19:05), so about 360 mL/h for the next 7 hours
opts.mark: Calculates fluids and times them from the burn
opts.r: Nurse Ko: 360 mL/h of warm Hartmann's, starting now.

opts.t: Urinary catheter; target 0.5 mL/kg/h (35 mL/h) and titrate
4 × 70 × 36 = 10,080 mL in 24 h (original Parkland)
opts.r: The ATLS 10th starting rate for adults is 2 mL/kg/%TBSA; 4 mL leads to fluid creep and compartment syndromes.

opts.t: TBSA 45% including the red face
Start the 8 hours from arrival in the ED
opts.r: The clock runs from the time of the burn. She is already an hour behind.

steps.label: Burn care
steps.hint: Cling film in strips, keep warm, elevate, watch the circumferential arm.

opts.t: Cling film laid in strips, not wrapped round the limbs
opts.mark: Covers with cling film laid in strips

opts.t: Elevate the burnt limbs
Check pulses in the right hand hourly: circumferential full-thickness burn
opts.mark: Monitors the circumferential burn for escharotomy

opts.t: Wrap cling film tightly around the right arm
opts.r: Wrapping acts as a tourniquet as the arm swells.

opts.t: Burst and debride the blisters now
opts.r: Leave it for the burns team.

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: Refer to the burns centre: size, full thickness, circumferential, inhalation.

opts.t: Burns centre: 36% TBSA, full-thickness circumferential right arm, inhalation injury, intubated, COHb 22%
opts.mark: Refers to the burns centre with the key criteria
opts.r: Burns consultant: Accept. Transfer when stable; call if the arm needs escharotomy first.

opts.t: Admit to the general surgical ward
opts.r: She meets several burns centre criteria.

steps.label: Handover
steps.hint: SBAR with times, TBSA, fluids and airway.

opts.t: SBAR: 30, burn 19:05, inhalation injury intubated, COHb 22%, 36% TBSA, Hartmann's 360 mL/h, UO target 35 mL/h, burns centre accepted
opts.mark: Structured handover with times, TBSA, fluids and plan
opts.r: The retrieval team repeat it back.

opts.t: Big burn, tubed, fluids on
opts.r: No size, no time, no rates.

qs.q: Which finding does NOT suggest inhalation injury?

wrong: The probe is on a burnt finger
CO shifts the curve to the right

qs.q: Which burns count toward TBSA for fluids?
Best way to estimate burn size in a child?
qs.why: Children's heads are proportionally larger and legs smaller than the adult rule of nines.

qs.q: Urine output target in an adult with burns?

rules.fail: You dressed wounds or calculated fluids while her airway was closing. Airway first.
rules.ok: Airway secured before the burn care.

badge.name: Fire Walker
badge.flavor: Tube early and uncut. Count from the burn, not the door.

cards.why: Half in the first 8 hours from the burn, the rest over 16; titrate to urine output.
cards.note: Original Parkland uses 4 mL; ATLS 10th starts adults at 2 mL.

cards.q: The first 8 hours of burn fluids are timed from…
cards.why: Any delay must be caught up.

cards.q: Carbon monoxide poisoning: SpO2 on a standard oximeter is…
cards.why: COHb absorbs light like oxyhaemoglobin at the oximeter's wavelengths. Use co-oximetry.

cards.q: Antidote for cyanide from smoke inhalation?
cards.why: It binds cyanide to form cyanocobalamin, excreted in urine.

cards.q: How should cling film be applied to a burnt arm?
options: Laid in strips along the limb
cards.why: Wrapping acts as a tourniquet as the limb swells.

cards.q: Urine output target in a child with major burns?
Which is NOT a burns centre referral criterion?
options: A 2% superficial (erythema) sunburn on the back
cards.why: Erythema is not counted and a small superficial burn is managed locally.
cards.source: ABA 2022; UK National Burn Care Referral Guidance
